verification_level: FAST plus BATCH plus the five affected SSL member-buffer/member-slot adversarial probes. Eight files audited, zero defects, zero repairs, no UB, no ABI regression and no hidden obligation. No file was deferred.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the eight head entries of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt: the SSL process-initialiser, the ssl_conf config driver, the deprecated RSA private-key spellings, the alert/state string readers, the session printers, the custom-extension registration surface, the TLS1.3 ServerHello extension block, and the protocol-version helpers. The two files flagged as possible init/callback boundaries were audited rather than deferred: ssl_init.rs introduces no ownership boundary of its own (it reuses the process-init contract), and extensions_srvr.rs invokes no application callback.
not_discharged: All audited files are file-level audits, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED and not SAFE_COMPATIBLE.
ssl_init.rs is audited against the existing process-init contract only; this receipt does not discharge the RUN_ONCE/initialisation ordering of the runtime init layer.

The custom-extension callbacks are stored but never invoked in this slice (no add/parse pass is walked). This receipt does not discharge their invocation contract, and no handshake path that calls them is exercised.
The TLS1.3 key-share constructor is audited for the non-resuming, non-HelloRetryRequest, X25519 arm only; the HRR and KEM arms remain unbuilt, and ssl_derive is not called.
No new cryptographic or timing evidence is claimed for the session printers or the key-share generation.
No Miri/ASan/Loom run was made: no owner, extent, aliasing or concurrency mechanism changed.
retained_obligations: src/ssl/ssl_init.rs: settings is NULL or a live OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS; the Once base step touches only the process-global compression registry and cannot fail.

src/ssl/ssl_mcnf.rs: exactly one of s/ctx is non-NULL (or both NULL for the refusal arm); name is NULL or NUL-terminated; the live object carries a live ctx/method. The final restores the previous default library context even when the switch never ran (NULL is a no-op).

src/ssl/ssl_rsa_legacy.rs: ssl/ctx is live and rsa is NULL or a live key; d is readable for len; file is NULL or NUL-terminated. Each RSA is up-reffed before EVP_PKEY_assign and released on every refusal, matching EVP_PKEY_assign's transfer-on-success contract.
src/ssl/ssl_stat.rs: s is NULL or a live connection; all returned strings are process-lifetime statics.
src/ssl/ssl_txt.rs: bp is a live writable BIO and x is NULL or a live session; bp's write callbacks must not free x during the call (the same C-level obligation the authority imposes).

src/ssl/statem/extensions_cust.rs: ctx is NULL or a live SSL_CTX and ctx->cert is non-NULL for every context this crate constructs (SSL_CTX_new refuses on cert_new failure); the callback pointers are stored, never invoked, and remain the application's to keep valid until the context is freed.

src/ssl/statem/extensions_srvr.rs: s is a live connection and pkt a live packet; the generated ephemeral key is transferred to s->pkey on success and freed on every failure, and SSL_free releases it once.
src/ssl/statem/statem_lib.rs: s is a live connection (a live Ssl always carries non-NULL method and cert); the out-pointers are writable, and real_max may be NULL.
residuals: extensions_cust.rs appends to the owned Vec with push/extend_from_slice; an allocator failure aborts the process where the authority's sk_CUSTOM_EXT_METHOD_push returns 0. This is the crate's established ownership-container behaviour, leaves no partially published record and is not UB; recorded rather than repaired.

extensions_srvr.rs assigns s->pkey directly, as the authority does. A second key-share construction on the same connection without an intervening clear would leak the previous key; the reduced state machine calls it once per handshake, so the path is unreachable here and matches the authority's own lifecycle assumption.

ssl_txt.rs indexes the fixed session_id/sid_ctx/master_key arrays by the stored length fields. A corrupted length panics (caught by guard_ffi) rather than reading out of bounds; the arrays are the authority's own extents.
ssl_mcnf.rs and extensions_cust.rs expose unguarded extern "C" exports. No panic is reachable for a contract-satisfying call (Vec push aside), so this is an observation, not a repair.
secret_bearing_buffers: ssl_rsa_legacy.rs imports and wraps private keys but copies no key material and changes no release path. ssl_txt.rs prints the session master key/PSK by design (the authority's own SSL_SESSION_print transcript). extensions_srvr.rs generates an ephemeral X25519 key and moves it into the connection's owned pkey slot; SSL_free remains its single release. No allocation, release coordinate or cleansing claim changed, and no constant-time property is asserted.
